findings.claim: Copying the request's `Content-Type` onto the rebuilt `Response` changes the `type` of blobs returned by `blob()` (and the effective media type for other representations) from `''` to the original media type, a silent behavior change for existing callers.
findings.rationale: Previously `new Response(body)` with a string/ArrayBuffer body produced a blob with an empty (or defaulted `text/plain;charset=UTF-8`) type; now `c.req.blob()` after another body accessor will return a Blob whose `type` is the full original header value including parameters (e.g. `multipart/form-data; boundary=...`). This is arguably more correct, but it is an observable change not limited to the `formData()` case the comment describes. Confidence: high that the behavior changes, medium that it matters to callers.

findings.claim: With the content type now preserved, `formData()` rebuilt from a `text`-cached body can silently produce corrupted/incorrect parts instead of failing fast.
findings.rationale: When the cached key is `text`, the original bytes were already decoded to a JS string; re-encoding that string as the body of a multipart/form-data response is lossy for binary file parts (and for any non-UTF-8 payload). Before this change such a call threw immediately because no content type was present; now it will parse and hand back plausible-looking but potentially corrupted `File` contents. Same concern applies when the cached key is `json`, where `JSON.stringify` produces bytes that differ from the original body while the original `Content-Type` is still advertised. Confidence: medium-high.

findings.claim: The truthiness check on `contentType` conflates an absent header with an empty-string header value.
findings.rationale: `raw.headers.get('content-type')` returns `null` when absent but `''` if the header is present and empty; both fall into the `undefined` branch. Functionally close to harmless, but an explicit `!== null` check would be more precise, and an empty string would otherwise be an invalid header value anyway. Low confidence that this has practical impact.
